title: Misty Sunrise
description: Photographer and National Geographic Explorer Carlton Ward Jr. wanted to get close as close as possible to these Florida cracker cattle on the pastures of the state's Buck Island Ranch. Using a wide angle lens, Ward witnessed the ranchers herding the cattle on horseback before dawn. “I was looking for the layering for the story,” he tells National Geographic. “Having the cowboy near the foreground is really important, but having the other cowboys in the background on the other side of the herd kind of helps make it a more immersive experience.” Ward's exhibition, "The Wild Path: Connecting the Florida We Don’t See,” is currently on display at the Orlando Museum of Art.
translated_description: 摄影师、国家地理探险家小卡尔顿·沃德想尽可能近距离地接触这些位于佛罗里达州巴克岛牧场上的佛罗里达 cracker 牛。使用广角镜头，沃德目睹了牧场主们在黎明前骑马放牧牛群。“我当时在寻找故事中的层次感，”他告诉《国家地理》。“让牛仔靠近前景非常重要，但让其他牛仔出现在牛群另一侧的背景中，也有助于营造一种更具沉浸感的体验。”沃德的展览“野性之路：连接我们看不见的佛罗里达”目前正在奥兰多艺术博物馆展出。
